messages:
lia: FYI — customer cust-9938 reporting intermittent embeddings shape flip after we pinned a variant to Reserved. They say vectors used to be 1536 but some responses are 768 since the pinned upgrade ~2h ago. attach: sample response and req_id.

elaine: thanks — can you paste the raw response + request id so I can escalate?

lia: here's the curl and the response we got from the customer (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...redacted' \\  -d '{"model":"redwood/embed-large@v3-pinned","input":"hello world"}'
```
response (truncated):
```json
{"request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d","model":"redwood/embed-large@v3-pinned","data":[{"embedding":[0.12,0.34,...],"length":768}]}
```
lia: Customer says it is intermittent — sometimes returns 1536 as expected, sometimes 768. Happens under their higher throughput tests.

sam: quick hypothesis: routing/fallback picked a different variant (quantized or smaller-arch) that produces 768 dims. On Dedicated/reserved pools we do automatic variant fallbacks when capacity/VM config mismatches. If the router selected a quantized variant that was built from a different model family, output dim can differ.

mike: any deploy events around that time?

deploy-bot: CANARY-ROLL: redwood/embed-large@v3 pinned -> reserved-pool at 2024-11-05T20:52:10Z (actor: infra-release)

jun: digging infra logs — I see batchpad/OOM events around the same window. batch controller fell back for some batches to `embed-large-qtz` due to transient GPU memory pressure. log excerpt: 
```
[2024-11-05T20:52:12Z] batchpad: request_batch_size=64, mem_avail=3.2GB, fallback_variant=embed-large-qtz
[2024-11-05T20:52:12Z] model_router: routed req=req_0a1b2c3d -> variant=embed-large-qtz
```
jun: `embed-large-qtz` was optimized/quantized and outputs 768 vectors in that build.

elaine: ok that matches the customer's symptom (intermittent, throughput-correlated). Immediate mitigation options?

mike: short term: force exact model version in the request (enforced version param) or disable automatic fallback for that customer. You can also reduce concurrency on their side. Example header to enforce variant: 
```json
{"model_variant": "redwood/embed-large:stable-1536"}
```
or send `?exact_version=true` in the request.

lia: I relayed the workaround and they confirmed setting explicit `model_variant` fixed it for their test run. They still want an explanation and a permanent fix.

sam: long term fix: router should validate output schema (embedding length) before sending to the client. If routed variant produces a different vector length than the requested model spec, we should either reject or remap to a compatible variant. Also add a guardrail that prevents fallback to variants with differing output schema.

ops-bot: INC-2026-142 created by mike: "Embeddings vector dim variance after reserved pool pin" severity: P2. Links: https://infra.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-142

jun: root-cause notes so far: pinned deployment reduced available mem headroom on certain GPUs -> batchpad tried to pack larger batch sizes -> runtime fallback to quantized variant that was available on that node. Fallback logic didn't check `output_dim` compatibility.

sam: suggested immediate code patch: add an `output_dim` attribute to model manifests and have the router assert equality before routing. Small change, should be a 1-2 day PR + canary. Also consider metric alerting: spike in mismatched-dim events.

elaine: I'll keep the customer updated. Lia, please add support ticket SUP-78391 and include the workaround.

lia: done — SUP-78391 created with incident link and mitigation notes. Customer replied: "Workaround applied, retested, looks good for now. Please confirm ETA for permanent fix."

sam: rough ETA for fix (router schema-check + manifest update + canary): 48-72 hours assuming no infra blockers. I'll own the PR; jun can help validate infra behavior.

mike: operational followups: 1) add emergency flag to disable fallback for single customer; 2) review autoscaler/batchpad to reduce batch size spikes during pinned rollouts.

lia: noted. I'll keep this thread updated. Closing loop here once sam posts the PR and we get a patch canary.

elaine: thanks all — great triage.

lia: customer will be notified that an eng fix is planned and SUP-78391 will get updates.

ops-bot: Ticket SUP-78391 linked to INC-2026-142.

mike: marking this resolved for support side, still tracking engineering remediation in INC.

lia: customer follow-up (from this morning): "We're back to normal with forced variant, but please let us know once a permanent check is in place so we can remove the workaround."

sam: will post PR link in this thread when created.

lia: end.
